stage_1_predict.prompt: Before calculating: When reflecting a point P(x, y) across the x-axis, which coordinate inverts its sign, and which coordinate remains invariant?
options: A. The x-coordinate inverts to -x; the y-coordinate is invariant.
B. The y-coordinate inverts to -y; the x-coordinate is invariant.
C. Both x and y invert their signs.
stage_1_predict.predict_rationale: Forces unassisted recall of horizontal vs vertical mirror isometries in the Cartesian plane before algebraic computation.

stage_2_attempt.task: In the attempt-box below, formulate the step-by-step solution: Point Q(7, -9) is reflected across the vertical y-axis to obtain point Q'. State the coordinates of Q', verify which quadrant Q' belongs to, and compute the distance between Q and Q'.

model_closure_revealed_post_attempt.step_1: Reflection across the vertical y-axis inverts the horizontal abscissa: (x, y) -> (-x, y). Therefore Q(7, -9) maps to Q'(-7, -9).
model_closure_revealed_post_attempt.step_2: In Q'(-7, -9), both x < 0 and y < 0. Thus Q' lies in Quadrant III.
model_closure_revealed_post_attempt.step_3: Distance QQ' = |7 - (-7)| = 14 units along the horizontal line y = -9.
model_closure_revealed_post_attempt.conclusion: The reflected point is Q'(-7, -9) in Quadrant III with distance QQ' = 14 units.

dialog_steps.inquiry: Working backwards: If two points have coordinates (x, y) and (-x, y), what is the equation of the line of symmetry that bisects the segment joining them?
dialog_steps.expected_insight: The vertical line x = 0 (the y-axis), which is the perpendicular bisector of the horizontal segment.

dialog_steps.inquiry: If you reflect a point across both axes sequentially (first x-axis, then y-axis), what single transformation is this equivalent to?
dialog_steps.expected_insight: Reflection across the origin: (x, y) -> (x, -y) -> (-x, -y), which is a half-turn (180° rotation) about (0,0).

stage_4_boundary_test.prompt: Boundary test on limiting case: Suppose point P lies directly on the axis of reflection, e.g., P(5, 0) reflected across the x-axis. What are the reflected coordinates?
options: A. (5, 0), because -0 = 0 and points lying on the line of reflection are invariant fixed points.
B. (-5, 0), because reflection always flips positive to negative.
D. Undefined, because axes do not have reflections.
stage_4_boundary_test.explanation: Points on the mirror line satisfy y = 0. Inverting y gives -0 = 0, so the point maps to itself: (5, 0) -> (5, 0). All points on the reflection axis are invariant fixed points of the isometry.

hint_1_conceptual_nudge.text: Identify which axis serves as the mirror line. Reflection across a coordinate axis negates the perpendicular coordinate while keeping the parallel coordinate unchanged.

hint_2_tactical_step.text: For vertical reflection across the y-axis, map (x, y) -> (-x, y). Thus Q(7, -9) becomes Q'(-7, -9). Because both points share the same ordinate y = -9, their separation is strictly |7 - (-7)| = 14 units.
